buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Scope of Supply Scope of supply (Bid price to include all cost components) : Supply Installation Testing and Commissioning of Goods 3. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Additional Terms & Conditions 1. The seller must submit a bid specific OEM Authorization Certificate. 2. The bidder shall submit a non blacklisting Affidavit duly signed and notarized. 3. GST Registration Certificate, PAN Card, Aadhar Card. 4. Bank Mandate Form. 5. MSME Certificate. 6. Product Datasheet. 7. CA Certified Turnover certificate. 8. Pre Bid Meet is Mandatory 9. Bank Solvency. OEM Eligibility Criteria 1 MAF will be required for all CCTV Items in favour of competent authority.

2 The OEM for cameras and NVRs must have its own company registered in India under the Compa nies Act, 1956/2013 for a minimum period of ten (10) years. Any representation through a dealer , distributor, or consortium shall not be considered as OEM eligibility. The same must be support ed with relevant statutory documents. Additionally, the CCTV OEM should have an operational manufacturing facility in India or globally for at least Seven (7) years. Documentary evidence in support of the same must be submitted. 3 OEM of CCTV should have minimum turnover of 200 crore to ensure that OEM is well established. 4 The CCTV OEM should have below ISO Certifications for Quality, Environment, Security managem ent and Health & Safety Management system for manufacturing of all types of Cameras & NVR. A ll the CCTV Components (Camera, NVR etc) should be from same OEM for seamless integration and ease of operation. The Bidder/s shall attach the copy of the OEM’s ISO Certificate along with the bid. ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 45001:2018, IEC 27032:2012, ISO 20000- 1:2018, ISO 50001:2018, CMMI Level 5 or above certification 5 All compliance for NVR and cameras will be required on OEM letter head along with product datasheets will be verified by the authority. 6 The OEM of the IP Cameras, NVR/VMS, Storage, and Network Switches shall not be blacklisted, d ebarred, or banned by any Government, Government Department, PSU, or Government agency i n India or abroad as on the date of bid submission. Preferably, all these components shall be fro m the same OEM. 7 OEM of the equipment/ solution shall have a positive Net Worth during last 3 years 8 CCTV OEM R&D Centre should be Registered with DSIR Lab. 9 The CCTV OEM must have supplied a minimum of 15,000 IP Cameras under a single Purchase Or der for CCTV surveillance of Government Schools/Colleges/ Universities/ Educational Institutions or under the Government Education vertical through any Central/State Government/ UT Administ ration/ PSU in India, as on the bid submission date. Copy of the P.O. along with valid supply/instal lation/completion proof shall be submitted with the technical bid. Experience of the CCTV OEM o nly shall be considered. 10 ONVIF should not have been suspended its support to the camera OEM & should be Full member of ONVIF not User that can be verified. 11 The Camera OEM should comply to General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). OEM should have valid EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility License/ Authorization No. from Central Pollution Co ntrol Board for Electrical & Electronic Equipment E-Waste. OEM need to submit its certificate with technical bid. 12 OEM Should be Listed in NSE/BSE Website. 13 To demonstrate the reliability and credibility of CCTV OEM, they must have supplied a minimum of 10,000 IP CCTV cameras to any State Government, Central Government, or Public Sector Und ertaking in India over the past ten years as of the bid submission date. Purchase order copies an d supply evidence should accompany the submission. 14 OEM Should have its Local Service Center in Jammu from last 5 years to ensure prompt after sale s service and spares to be readily available. Documentary proof Required. 15 Bid Specific OEM authorisation for major components -CCTV System, Switches, Cable and Racks should be uploaded along with bid, non-submission of any one of these will be rejected without any specific reason.

16 Non malicious code is present in the hardware and software self-certification from OEM required. 17 The OEM of the CCTV camera must have more than 800 employees on its payroll in India. This is to justify that CCTV OEM has made investment in India and is serious about its business in India which will ensure long term after sales support and spare support from the OEM. Respectiv e document/ certificate to be provided along with the bid. .
